Enquiries show that the office of the "Banque Franco-Manchou"
was established in Room 309, No. 2 Peking Road (Glen Line Blg.)
in March of the current year by a certain S. D. Rubinstein, a
naturalized Portuguese of Russian-Jewish origin, who visited
Shanghai recently. He is reported to be the son of D. L. Rubin-
stein, a financier, who was well known in pre-revolutionary
Petrograd and who shortly prior to the Russian revolution
established the "Franco-Russian Bank" in that city. His death
in Zagreb, Jugoslavia, was recently announced in the local
Russian newspapers.

S. D. Rubinstein is the head of the "Banque Franco-Asiatique",
the main office of which is reported to be in Paris and which
has branch offices in Harbin and Tokio. Mr. N.D. Bouianovsky,
Russian, who committed suicide recently, was the manager of the
Harbin branch of the bank in question, while Mr. A. Massenet,
French, is the director of the Tokio branch. It appears that
Mr. Rubinstein-Junior also had an office in Paris under the
name of "Banque Franco-Manchou" and that he has a considerable
interest in a certain mining concern in Korea. It is rumoured
that about six months ago he was requested to leave Paris as
the French government objected to his activities on the local
Exchange (speculating on fall of the franc).

Rubinstein arrived in Shanghai from Europe via Japan-Harbin
on February 10. He took up his residence at the Cathay Hotel
where apartment No. 513 had been reserved for him by Mr. Ellis
Hayim of the Cathay Land Co. Ltd., to whom Rubinstein is
reported to be well known. Towards the end of February
Mr. Massenet also arrived here. He occupied apartment 502 at
the same hotel. The following individuals who resided at the

调查显示，“法满银行”办事处由一名名为 S. D. 鲁宾斯坦的人于今年三月在北京路2号（格兰轮船公司大楼）309室设立。此人是俄裔犹太籍归化葡萄牙人，最近访问了上海。据报他是 D. L. 鲁宾斯坦之子，D. L. 鲁宾斯坦是一位金融家，在革命前的彼得格勒颇有名气，并在俄国革命前夕在该市建立了“法俄银行”。当地俄文报纸最近刊登了他死于南斯拉夫萨格勒布的消息。

S. D. 鲁宾斯坦是“法亚银行”（Banque Franco-Asiatique）的首脑，据报该银行总行设在巴黎，并在哈尔滨和东京设有分行。最近自杀的俄国人 N.D. 布亚诺夫斯基先生是该银行哈尔滨分行的经理，而法国人 A. 马塞内特先生则是东京分行的行长。看来小鲁宾斯坦先生在巴黎也以“法满银行”的名义设有一个办事处，并且他在朝鲜某矿业公司中拥有相当大的利益。有谣言称，大约六个月前，他被要求离开巴黎，因为法国政府反对他在当地交易所的活动（投机法郎下跌）。

鲁宾斯坦于2月10日经日本-哈尔滨从欧洲抵达上海。他在华懋饭店入住，该饭店513号公寓已由华懋地产有限公司的海伊姆先生为他预留，据报鲁宾斯坦与海伊姆先生相识已久。二月底，马塞内特先生也抵达此处。他入住了同一家饭店的502号公寓。以下人士当时也居住在

SENSATIONAL CASE OF SERGE RUBINSTEIN

He is charged with a series of misappropriations

A sensational case against Serge RUBINSTEIN, banker
and financier, will soon be heard at the Supreme Court in
New York.

The case was brought against him by two shareholders
of the "Chosen Corporation Limited", a British concern which
owned gold mines in Korea.

Apart from Rubinstein and certain of his associates
a number of concerns, which were or still are under his con-
trol, are involved in this affair.

In particular, Rubinstein is accused of having mis-
appropriated the funds of the "Chosen Corporation". His acti-
vities in connection with this matter took place in almost eve-
ry country in the world - France, England, Korea, Japan, Manchu-
ria, United States and Latin America.

According to the complaint, the method applied by Ru-
binstein was very simple. He acquired control over a concern.
Later he exchanged the shares of the concern for those of a
bogus concern created specially for the purpose and having no
capital whatever. Some time afterwards the bogus concern was
liquidated. All the valuable shares remained in Rubinstein's
possession. According to the complaint, all these activities
were outwardly within the limits of law, so that an investi-
gation committee of the London Board of Trade could do nothing
in this respect.

"A Portuguese from Russia"

Rubinstein asserts that he is a Portuguese citizen.
However, it is known that he arrived in the United States as
a Russian. At present he calls himself Serge Manuel de Royal.

（批：File）
（印：MAY 28 1941 / SPECIAL BRANCH）
（批：28 5 41）

谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦的轰动案件

他被指控犯有一系列挪用公款罪

针对银行家兼金融家谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦的一起轰动性案件即将在纽约最高法院审理。

此案由“朝鲜株式会社”（Chosen Corporation Limited）的两名股东对他提起，这是一家拥有朝鲜金矿的英国公司。

除了鲁宾斯坦及其某些同伙外，许多受他控制或曾经受他控制的公司也卷入此事。

特别是，鲁宾斯坦被指控挪用“朝鲜株式会社”的资金。他在此事上的活动几乎遍及世界各国——法国、英国、朝鲜、日本、满洲、美国和拉丁美洲。

根据诉状，鲁宾斯坦使用的方法非常简单。他取得了一家公司的控制权。随后，他将该公司的股份交换为专门为此目的创建的、毫无资本的虚假公司的股份。一段时间后，该虚假公司被清算。所有有价值的股份都留在了鲁宾斯坦手中。据诉状称，所有这些活动在表面上都在法律允许范围内，因此伦敦贸易委员会的调查委员会对此无能为力。

“来自俄罗斯的葡萄牙人”

鲁宾斯坦声称自己是葡萄牙公民。然而，众所周知，他是作为俄罗斯人抵达美国的。目前他自称塞尔日·曼努埃尔·德·罗亚尔。

（批：归档）

Apart from the "Chosen Corporation" the complaint mentions its two branches in Korea - the "Nuruki Koban Kabushiki Kaisha" and "Kapan Kosan KK", four French Banks - Henry Dupont, Franco-Asiatic, Franco-Manchou and "Societe Financiere Internationale" and also about twenty various joint-stock companies.

The following persons are mentioned in the complaint as being bogus personages: Baron Joseph de Gotch(?), Gustav Rau(?), Andrew Rubinstein ( brother of Serge ), Alfred Massenet ( nephew of Massenet, the composer, an engineer in the Korean concerns ), Paul Klopfstock, Duke of Chartre (?), Prince Eugene Gagarin and others. Rubinstein started his career as head of the Chosen Corporation at the time when the career of Harman, the "King of Landy(?) Island," ended.

"King Harman"

Many people still remember how Harman acquired the ownership of the Landy Island and declared himself a feudal prince. He claimed the right of coining his own money. Harman pence appeared in London, but the government interfered and put an end to this affair. Two years afterwards Harman was charged with misappropriation of the capital of the "Chosen Corporation". During the course of the trial of this case various shady affairs of Harman came to light. Harman was arrested. He handed over the control of the "Chosen Corporation" to Serge Rubinstein. The latter by means of various manipulations acquired the ownership of the larger part of shares without paying a cent.

Rubinstein "compelled" the "Chosen Corporation" to lend £300.000 to the "British-American Equities" - a concern established by him, and later created a number of concerns in

诉状中提到的下列人员被视为虚构人物：约瑟夫·德·戈奇男爵(?)、古斯塔夫·劳(?)、安德鲁·鲁宾斯坦（谢尔盖的兄弟）、阿尔弗雷德·马塞内特（作曲家马塞内的侄子，朝鲜各公司的工程师）、保罗·克洛夫斯托克、沙特尔公爵(?)、叶夫根尼·加加林亲王等。鲁宾斯坦在“兰迪岛(?)之王”哈曼的职业生涯结束时，开始了自己作为朝鲜株式会社负责人的职业生涯。

“哈曼国王”

许多人仍然记得哈曼如何获得兰迪岛的所有权并自封为封建亲王。他声称有权铸造自己的货币。哈曼便士曾在伦敦出现，但政府介入并终结了此事。两年后，哈曼被指控挪用“朝鲜株式会社”的资本。在此案的审判过程中，哈曼的各种 shady（原文不清/可疑）事务曝光。哈曼被捕。他将“朝鲜株式会社”的控制权移交给谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦。后者通过各种手段，未付分文便获得了大部分股份的所有权。

鲁宾斯坦“迫使”“朝鲜株式会社”向他建立的“英美股权公司”（British-American Equities）贷款300,000英镑，随后在美国创建了许多公司，

谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦的重大案件。
他被指控犯有一系列盗窃罪行。
这是一起重大案件，在完全合法的框架内，一位臭名昭著的银行家和金融家——所谓的哈曼“国王”、系统主义者谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦的案件即将在纽约最高法院审理。伦敦贸易局调查委员会并未取得任何成果。许多人记得，哈曼是如何买下兰迪岛的，因为他知道现在他是封建亲王，并有权依法铸造自己的货币。当时英国出现了哈曼便士，但政府介入并制止了此事。两年后，哈曼因“侵吞‘乔文’公司资本”而被起诉。[在审判过程中] 揭露了他的各种欺诈行为。哈曼被捕。他将控制权移交给了谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦。后者通过各种手段获得了该公司的巨大权力，而未花费分文。

两名“乔文有限公司”（一家拥有朝鲜金矿的英国公司）的股东对S.鲁宾斯坦提起诉讼。案件中不仅涉及鲁宾斯坦及其某些同伙，还涉及一系列处于或曾处于其控制下的公司。特别是，鲁宾斯坦被指控盗用“乔文有限公司”的资源。其行为几乎遍及世界各地——法国、英国、朝鲜、日本、满洲、美国以及拉丁美洲。

根据诉状，“鲁宾斯坦的方法”非常简单。他取得某家公司的控制权。然后承诺支付巨额款项，以换取由他管理该公司。但是，拿到钱后，他便消失无踪，留下陷入全面混乱的公司。“乔文公司”如此，其他公司亦然。

鲁宾斯坦声称自己是葡萄牙公民，但众所周知，他是通过俄罗斯配额进入美国的。他现在自称塞尔日·马努埃尔·鲁宾斯坦·德·罗维洛。（其中提到的除了“乔文公司”及其两个朝鲜分支机构“Nafuki Koban Kabushiki Kaisha”和“Kapan Kovan KK”外，还有四家法国银行：亨利·杜邦、法亚银行、法满银行和“国际金融社”，以及二十多家股份公司。）这些人的名字如下：约瑟夫·德·贡茨男爵、格拉姆·福（主席）、安德烈·马萨尔……

S.D. RUBINSTEIN

Sergey Dimitrievich RUBINSTEIN, Russian of Jewish
origin, was born on May 31, 1908 at Kronstadt, Russia.
He is the son of D.L. Rubinstein, internationally
known financier, famous in Russia prior to the
revolution for his speculations. The elder Rubinstein,
who among other enterprises founded the Franco-Russian
Bank at Petrograd, died at Zagreb (Jugoslavia) in
either 1935 or 1936. S.D. Rubinstein is reported to
have left Russia many years ago and to have been
educated in England. Some time later he became a
naturalized Portuguese citizen.

Rubinstein first came to notice of the Municipal
Police early in 1936. Coming from Europe, he arrived
in Shanghai on February 10, 1936 via Japan and Harbin..
He stayed at Room 513 Cathay Hotel which was reserved
for him by Mr. Ellis Hayim of the Cathay Land Company,
who is believed to have known Rubinstein for a long
period of time. He was reported to be the head of
the "Banque Franco-Asiatique" in Paris, which had
branches in Tokyo and Harbin. Towards the end of
February Rubinstein was joined by Mr. A. Massenet
(1) from Japan, who put up at the same hotel, Room
No. 502. During his stay in Shanghai Rubinstein was
reported to have been in contact with several persons
including Messrs. J. Gadsby, (2) J.C. Gruner and J.
Guilbert, (3) also residing at the Cathay Hotel.
Rubinstein with Guilbert left Shanghai on March 8, 1936
for New York via Vancouver by the s.s. "Empress of
Japan". Leaving on the same vessel for the United
States, was the Countess Nathalie Rostovtzeff, nee M.
Bogdanova, Rubinstein's mistress. She arrived in
Shanghai on February 28, 1936 on the s.s. "Hakone
Maru" and resided at the

S.D. 鲁宾斯坦

谢尔盖·季米特里耶维奇·鲁宾斯坦，俄裔犹太人，1908年5月31日出生于俄罗斯喀琅施塔得。他是D.L. 鲁宾斯坦之子，后者是国际知名的金融家，在革命前的俄罗斯因其投机活动而闻名。老鲁宾斯坦除其他企业外，还在彼得格勒创立了法俄银行，于1935年或1936年在萨格勒布（南斯拉夫）去世。据报道，S.D. 鲁宾斯坦多年前离开俄罗斯，并在英国接受教育。不久后，他成为归化葡萄牙公民。

鲁宾斯坦首次引起工部局警务处注意是在1936年初。他从欧洲出发，经日本和哈尔滨，于1936年2月10日抵达上海。他住在汇中饭店513室，该房间由汇中地产公司的埃利斯·海伊姆先生为他预订，据信海伊姆先生认识鲁宾斯坦已有很长时间。据报道，他是巴黎“法亚银行”的行长，该银行在东京和哈尔滨设有分行。2月底，A. 马塞内特先生(1)从日本来沪与他汇合，入住同一家酒店的502室。据报道，鲁宾斯坦在上海期间与数人有接触，包括同样居住在汇中饭店的J. 加兹比先生(2)、J.C. 格鲁纳和J. 吉尔伯特(3)。鲁宾斯坦与吉尔伯特于1936年3月8日乘“日本皇后号”轮船经温哥华前往纽约。同船前往美国的还有娜塔莉·罗斯托夫采娃伯爵夫人，娘家姓M. 博格达诺娃，系鲁宾斯坦的情妇。她于1936年2月28日乘“箱根丸”轮抵达上海，居住在

During this stay in Shanghai Rubinstein opened,
on March 15, 1936, the "Banque Franco-Manchou" at 2
Peking Road (Room 309). The room in question was
partitioned into two or three offices and had the
appearance of being only of a temporary nature. Mr.
Rubinstein refused to sign a lease and paid his rent
($220) monthly. The staff of the organisation
comprised only a stenographer, a certain Mrs. V.A.
Selivanovsky, Russian. She was also Rubinstein's
secretary and was recommended to him by Mr. Kahn,
exchange broker and financial expert, who is well
known in Shanghai.

According to Rubinstein, the capital of the
"Banque Franco-Manchou" was about Fcs. 1,500,000.
The information to hand does not permit it to be
stated exactly whether this was a question of the
transfer to Shanghai of the administrative offices
of bank already in existence, or the creation, pure
and simple, of a new concern. It was reported, under
reserve, that this bank was established by Rubinstein
to facilitate his operations with the "Chosen
Corporation" because the financial standing of the
Franco-Asiatic Bank, of which he was Managing Director,
was somewhat precarious. The new bank, it was reported,
intended issuing exploitation claims for alluvial
gold located in the mouth of the Sungari, upon which
Rubinstein had obtained an option through the good
offices of a cousin of the Emperor Kang Teh (Henry
Pu Yi).

On May 21, 1936 Rubinstein arrived in Shanghai
from Tientsin by plane and stayed at the Cathay Hotel
(Ext. 88/4) until May 28, 1936, whence left for Hong

此次在上海停留期间，鲁宾斯坦于1936年3月15日在北京路2号（309室）开设了“法满银行”。该房间被隔成两三个办公室，看起来只是临时性质的。鲁宾斯坦先生拒绝签署租赁合同，按月支付租金（220美元）。该机构的工作人员仅有一名速记员，即V.A. 塞利瓦诺夫斯基太太，俄罗斯人。她也是鲁宾斯坦的秘书，由在上海颇有名气的汇率经纪人和金融专家卡恩先生推荐给他。

据鲁宾斯坦称，“法满银行”的资本约为150万法郎。现有资料无法确切说明这是将一家已存在银行的行政办事处迁至上海，还是纯粹创建了一家新机构。据传闻（有待证实），鲁宾斯坦成立这家银行是为了便利其与“乔文公司”的业务往来，因为他担任董事总经理的法亚银行的财务状况有些岌岌可危。据报道，这家新银行打算发行位于松花江口冲积金的开采权，鲁宾斯坦已通过康德皇帝（溥仪）的一位表亲的斡旋获得了该期权。

1936年5月21日，鲁宾斯坦乘飞机从天津抵达上海，住在汇中饭店（分机 88/4），直至1936年5月28日离开前往香港

- 3 -

in the company of Mrs. Selivanovsky. Countess Erdödy,
who arrived in Shanghai from Tientsin by rail on May 24,
1936 and stayed at the same hotel, left for Vancouver
on May 31, 1936 in the s.s. "Empress of Canada".

Practically no signs of any business activities
were noticed at the office of the "Banque Franco-
Manchou". Some time towards the end of 1936 the office
was removed from Room 309 to Room 510 and subsequently
to Room 507 in the same building. The new office was
even smaller than the original one. Mrs. Selivanovsky
attended the office very irregularly, often leaving it
in charge of a Chinese office boy. Between November
25 and December 8, 1936 she made a trip to Japan.

Rubinstein returned to Shanghai on December 19,
1936 coming from the North by rail. He stayed at the
Cathay Hotel until the beginning of January, 1937 when
he left for Peking. He was back in Shanghai about the
middle of the same month. During this period the local
Russian newspaper "Shanghai Zaria" published two
articles evidently inspired by Rubinstein, in which the
latter's plans of future activities were outlined
(Vide Appendices "A" and "B").

On February 2, 1937 a mild sensation was created
in Shanghai by the news that Rubinstein had suddenly
left for Japan in the s.s. "Nagasaki Maru" in the company
of a certain Miss Gloria SEITER, aged 19, American, a
cabaret dancer who had been performing at Ciro's Night
Club. Their sudden departure gave rise to rumours of
an elopement and they were nicknamed "Svengali and Trilby".
Interviewed upon arrival at Nagasaki and later at Tokyo
both Rubinstein and Miss Seiter denied their intention

同行者为塞利瓦诺夫斯基太太。厄尔多迪伯爵夫人于1936年5月24日乘火车从天津抵达上海，入住同一家酒店，并于1936年5月31日乘“加拿大皇后号”轮船前往温哥华。

在“法满银行”办事处几乎未观察到任何商业活动的迹象。1936年底左右，办事处从309室搬至同一栋楼的510室，随后又搬至507室。新办事处甚至比原来的还要小。塞利瓦诺夫斯基太太很少去办事处，经常将其交给一名中国听差照看。1936年11月25日至12月8日期间，她前往日本旅行。

鲁宾斯坦于1936年12月19日乘火车从北方返回上海。他在汇中饭店住到1937年1月初，随后前往北平。他在当月月中左右回到上海。在此期间，当地俄文报纸《上海霞光报》发表了两篇显然受鲁宾斯坦指使的文章，概述了他未来的活动计划（见附录“A”和“B”）。

1937年2月2日，一则消息在上海引起轻微轰动：鲁宾斯坦突然与19岁的美国歌舞女郎格洛丽亚·赛特小姐一同乘“长崎丸”轮前往日本，赛特小姐此前曾在西罗夜总会表演。他们的突然离去引发了私奔的谣言，他们被戏称为“斯文加利和特里尔比”。鲁宾斯坦和赛特小姐在抵达长崎及后来在东京接受采访时均否认了

of marrying. Rubinstein was quoted as saying that he
intended to take Miss Seiter to Europe "to make her
one of the world's greatest dancers". According to
press reports, Miss Seiter sailed from Yokohama for
Seattle on February 9, 1937 in the s.s. "Hikawa Maru",
while Rubinstein remained in Japan and is believed

The latest information on record regarding
Rubinstein is contained in an article which appeared
in the local Russian newspaper "Novosti Dnia" on
November 20, 1937 (Appendix "C"), according to which
Rubinstein sold the "Chosen Corporation" to the
Japanese and left for London to attend the annual
meeting of shareholders.

The local office of the "Banque-Franco Manchou"
was closed some time towards the end of 1937, following
the outbreak of Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai.
Mrs. Selivanovsky is now employed with the Union
Commercial Company, 320 Szechuen Road. According to
her, Rubinstein is believed to be in the United States
at present.

During his stay in Shanghai Rubinstein was the
subject of enquiries originating from several sources.

结婚的意图。据引述，鲁宾斯坦表示他打算带赛特小姐去欧洲，“使她成为世界上最伟大的舞者之一”。据新闻报道，赛特小姐于1937年2月9日乘“冰川丸”轮从横滨驶往西雅图，而鲁宾斯坦则留在日本，据信后来也访问了朝鲜。后来有报道称，他与由已故贵族院议员井上恭次郎子爵组成的一群日本资本家讨论日本参与为华北金矿开采业务融资的国际财团的可能性。

关于鲁宾斯坦的最新存档信息见于1937年11月20日当地俄文报纸《今日新闻》上发表的一篇文章（附录“C”），文中称鲁宾斯坦将“乔文公司”出售给日本人，并前往伦敦参加年度股东大会。

随着上海中日敌对行动的爆发，“法满银行”当地办事处于1937年底左右关闭。塞利瓦诺夫斯基太太目前受雇于四川路320号的联合商业公司。据她说，鲁宾斯坦据信目前在美国。

鲁宾斯坦在上海停留期间，成为来自多个渠道查询的对象。继工部局警务处对他在使用期间的保险箱中被窃大量钱财的指控进行调查后

page_data.en:
- 5 -

stay at the Cathay Hotel, the proprietors instituted
enquiries in London regarding his antecedents. The
reply received indicated that Rubinstein was regarded in
financial circles in the City as a sharp financier of
doubtful character, whose business methods would not
bear close scrutiny.

A report from London gives the following
particulars regarding Rubinstein's antecedents and
activities :

"Serge Rubinstein is reported to have been
educated in England and to have first arrived in
France in 1928. He entered the Banque Franco-Asiatique
in Paris as Secretary to the Managing Director and
soon, with the help and advice of his father, occupied
a preponderating position in this financial concern,
which, until its liquidation soon after, was known
as the Banque Russo-Asiatique. In June, 1932 he was
made a member of the Board of Directors of the Banque
Franco-Asiatique, which had been founded as a limited
liability company for commercial, industrial and real
estate transactions in France and abroad, but chiefly
in Manchoukuo. The Bank, however, was believed to be
unfavourably regarded in both Paris and London. When
he was made a member of the Board of Directors many
shareholders protested as it was felt that both he and
his father were merely using the Bank as a convenient
instrument for dealing with several risky and adventurous
undertakings.

In 1933 Serge Rubinstein was reported as the
Managing Director of the Chemo Corporation Ltd., 60
Moorgate, E.C.2. The business of this firm was the

入住华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）时，业主方面在伦敦对其背景进行了调查。收到的回复表明，鲁宾斯坦（Rubinstein）在伦敦金融城（City）的金融圈中被视为一名手段精明但品行可疑的金融家，其商业手法经不起仔细审查。

一份来自伦敦的报告提供了以下关于鲁宾斯坦背景和活动的详情：

“据称，谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦（Serge Rubinstein）在英国接受教育，并于1928年首次抵达法国。他进入巴黎的法亚银行（Banque Franco-Asiatique），担任总经理秘书，并很快在其父亲的帮助和建议下，在该金融机构中占据了主导地位；该机构在不久后清算之前，被称为俄亚银行（Banque Russo-Asiatique）。1932年6月，他被任命为法亚银行董事会成员，该银行作为一家有限责任公司成立，旨在从事法国及海外的商业、工业和房地产交易，但主要是在满洲国。然而，据信该银行在巴黎和伦敦均声誉不佳。当他被任命为董事会成员时，许多股东提出抗议，因为人们认为他和他的父亲仅仅是利用该银行作为处理几项高风险和投机性企业的便利工具。

1933年，据报谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦是位于伦敦E.C.2区穆尔盖特街60号（60 Moorgate, E.C.2）的凯莫公司有限公司（Chemo Corporation Ltd.）的总经理。该公司的业务是

page_data.en:

exploitation of gold, silver and other mines on the
Chinese.Korean boundary. Those in charge of the
Corporation were said to be in very favourable
relations with the Government of Manchoukuo.

Rubinstein was reported to be an unscrupulous
man in the City of London and alleged to have been
under suspicion of espionage in France in 1933.
His father is said to have been sentenced to a
term of imprisonment at Paris for heavy commercial
frauds".

An extract from a report, dated April, 1936,
from French sources reads as follows :-

"Serge Rubinstein is one of the directors of
the Banque Franco-Asiatique which was created in
Paris following the failure of the Banque Russo-
Asiatique. This bank has two branches, one in
Tokyo, which is directed by Mr. A. MASSENET, and
the other at Harbin. The director of the latter
branch, Mr. M.D. BOULANOVSKY, committed suicide
several months ago in Harbin, and it is thought in
Russian circles there that his death was brought
about by the bad state of affairs of the bank.

In 1932, when Rubinstein was in Europe, he
was informed by a friend that if he had a million
francs to dispose, he could acquire in London the
control of an excellent gold-mine in Korea, the
"Chosen Corporation", formed by Mr. BORDON.

Rubinstein, who could only muster Frs. 300,
000, obtained the balance of Frs. 700,000 from the
Banque Franco-Asiatique, on whose behalf he had to
complete the negotiations.

开发中朝边境的金矿、银矿和其他矿山。据说该公司负责人与满洲国政府关系非常良好。

据报鲁宾斯坦在伦敦金融城是一个肆无忌惮的人，并被指控于1933年在法国涉嫌从事间谍活动。据说他的父亲因重大商业欺诈罪在巴黎被判监禁”。

摘自1936年4月法国来源的一份报告摘录如下：-

“谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦是法亚银行的董事之一，该银行是在俄亚银行倒闭后在巴黎成立的。该银行有两个分行，一个在东京，由A. 马塞内特（A. MASSENET）先生主管，另一个在哈尔滨。后一分行的行长M.D. 布拉诺夫斯基（M.D. BOULANOVSKY）先生几个月前在哈尔滨自杀，当地的俄罗斯圈子认为，他的死是由该银行糟糕的经营状况造成的。

1932年，当鲁宾斯坦在欧洲时，一位朋友告诉他，如果他有一百万法郎可供支配，他可以在伦敦收购一家名为‘朝鲜公司’（Chosen Corporation）的优质韩国金矿的控制权，该公司由博尔东（BORDON）先生组建。

鲁宾斯坦只能凑集30万法郎，他从法亚银行获得了剩余的70万法郎，他代表该银行完成了谈判。

- 7 -

Rubinstein to the London banker HARMAN (4) who, as
the holder of stocks of many concerns and in particular
of those of the "Chosen Corporation", had on deposit
in his bank large sums of money for these enterprises,
which he is believed to have embezzled and which he
endeavoured to bolster-up whilst negotiating with
the shares in his possession.

When Rubinstein met Harman, "Chosen Corporation"
shares were standing at about 7/-. With his million
francs, Rubinstein bought :-

1) from Harman or his group - 125,000 "Chosen"
for cash, and

2) at the same time, on credit, 125,000 "Chosen"
which Harman had sold for 15/- to certain
Japanese companies, and promised to pay
16/6d. for them. Thus he got possession
of 250,000 shares at an average of 12/3d.

With the 125,000 shares purchased from Harman
Rubinstein, with another stockbroking concern,
created a market for the stock, which rapidly rose
in value, permitting him to pay the Japanese companies
the extra 1/6d. per share.

Later, Rubinstein acquired an option on about
170,000 new shares at 22/- which made his total
holdings about 420,000. The amount of stock he is
at present carrying is unknown, but it is reported
that he owns at least two-thirds of "Chosen" stock.

The advantage over other shareholders conferred
on him by virtue of the amount of stock in his
possession allowed Rubinstein to "call himself" the
Managing Director of the "Chosen" Mines to the tune
of an annual salary of a million francs plus his
travelling expenses.

After these financial operations Rubinstein
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

鲁宾斯坦与伦敦银行家哈曼（HARMAN）(4)接洽，后者作为许多企业股票、特别是‘朝鲜公司’股票的持有者，在其银行中存有这些企业的大量资金，据信他挪用了这些资金，并试图通过谈判处理其持有的股票来掩盖这一事实。

当鲁宾斯坦会见哈曼时，‘朝鲜公司’的股价约为7先令。鲁宾斯坦用他的一百万法郎购买了：

1) 从哈曼或其集团手中以现金购买125,000股‘朝鲜公司’股票，以及

2) 同时以赊购方式购买125,000股‘朝鲜公司’股票，哈曼已以15先令的价格将这些股票出售给某些日本公司，并承诺以16先令6便士的价格回购。因此，他以平均12先令3便士的价格获得了250,000股。

利用从哈曼处购买的125,000股，鲁宾斯坦与另一家股票经纪公司一起为该股票创造了市场，股价迅速上涨，使他能够向日本公司支付每股额外的1先令6便士。

后来，鲁宾斯坦获得了以22先令购买约170,000股新股的选择权，使其总持股量达到约420,000股。他目前持有的股票数量不详，但有报道称他至少拥有‘朝鲜公司’三分之二的股票。

凭借其持有的大量股票所赋予的优于其他股东的优势，鲁宾斯坦得以‘自称’为‘朝鲜’矿业的总经理，年薪高达一百万法郎，外加差旅费。

在这些金融操作之后，鲁宾斯坦

page_data.en:
- 8 -

made his way to Korea. The other holders of stock,
especially English holders, furious at being "skinned"
in this manner, had an engineer sent to the "Chosen"
Mines in order to examine them and make a report
discrediting their worth. This report, made public,
would have had the effect of lowering the value of
the shares, thus permitting the English shareholders
to recoup themselves by buying stock that Rubinstein
could not fail to place upon the market. Indeed the
report was published and the shares did drop. But
Rubinstein, however, was not to be duped by this
piece of strategy, and on the contrary, profited
from this drop in prices by buying more shares
instead of selling his own, for during his stay in
Korea he had taken the opportunity to gather information
regarding the yield of the mine, which was in the
neighbourhood of Y. 160,000 per month. Later, he
was responsible for having another report made,
favouring the "Chosen" Mine, by Mr. A. Massenet, a
well known engineer, who was acting in good faith.
The results of this report were soon forthcoming,
and the value of the "Chosen" stock went up. This
series of operations thus brought Rubinstein a very
considerable profit.

It should be stated, however, that Rubinstein
enjoys the reputation of being an astute speculator.
He was expelled from France in 1933 for speculating
in francs, but the expulsion decree was rescinded
some months later following pleas made on his behalf.

(1) Mr. Alfred MASSENET, French engineer and
financier, has been in the Far East
for many years. Is married to a Japanese lady.
Massenet, former well known Parisian stock

前往朝鲜。其他股票持有人，尤其是英国持有人，对以这种方式被‘剥皮’（遭受损失）感到愤怒，派遣了一名工程师前往‘朝鲜’矿业进行检查，并制作了一份贬低其价值的报告。这份公开的报告本会导致股价下跌，从而使英国股东能够通过购买鲁宾斯坦不得不投放市场的股票来弥补损失。确实，报告发表了，股价也确实下跌了。但是，鲁宾斯坦并没有被这种策略所欺骗，相反，他利用价格下跌的机会购买了更多股票，而不是卖出自己的股票，因为在朝鲜停留期间，他趁机收集了有关矿产量的信息，月产量约为16万日元。后来，他委托著名工程师A. 马塞内特（A. Massenet）先生制作了另一份有利于‘朝鲜’矿业的报告，马塞内特先生是出于善意行事的。这份报告的结果很快显现，‘朝鲜’股票的价值随之上升。这一系列操作从而给鲁宾斯坦带来了非常可观的利润。

然而，必须指出的是，鲁宾斯坦享有精明投机者的声誉。他曾于1933年因炒作法郎被驱逐出法国，但在为其提出的请求之后，几个月后驱逐令被撤销。

Appendix "A"

Summarized translation of an interview with S.D.
Rubinstein published in the "Shanghai Zaris" on
December 22, 1936.

Mr. S.D. Rubinstein is Chairman of the Governing
Board of a big goldmining corporation in Japan and
Korea and besides acts as Director-General of three
financial concerns in London and one in Paris.

He arrived from London to the Far East recently
and intends to remain here for another month, after
which he will return to Europe, the main field of
his activities.

Up to the current year the goldmining corporation
which Mr. Rubinstein plans to develop in the Far East,
has been active only in Japan and Korea. Now it is
planned to include Manchoukuo and North China in the
sphere of its activities.

Work was already started in North China during
August last under the supervision of Mr. Massenet,
engineer, while a Russian engineer named Vodennikoff
is in charge of the work in Manchoukuo. General
Horvath's son is Secretary of the Governing Board of
the Corporation in North China. The staff of the
corporation and the majority of workers are Russians.

Mr. Rubinstein is also the representative of
holders of unpaid coupons of the Russian part of the
"Reorganization Loan" issued by the Chinese Government
in 1913. In order to secure the payment of these
coupons he intends to proceed to Nanking on December
22, where he will interview representatives of the
Ministry of Finance, after which he will make a trip
to North China. Upon his return to Shanghai Mr.
Rubinstein will leave for Europe.

附录“A”

1936年12月22日刊登在《上海柴拉报》（Shanghai Zaris）上的对S.D. 鲁宾斯坦采访的摘要译文。

S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生是日本和朝鲜一家大型金矿公司的管理委员会主席，此外还担任伦敦三家金融机构和巴黎一家金融机构的总干事。

他最近从伦敦来到远东，打算在此再停留一个月，之后将返回欧洲，那里是他活动的主要领域。

直到今年，鲁宾斯坦先生计划在远东发展的金矿公司仅在日本和朝鲜开展业务。现在计划将满洲国和华北纳入其业务范围。

去年八月，在马塞内特工程师的监督下，华北的工作已经开始，而一位名叫沃登尼科夫（Vodennikoff）的俄罗斯工程师负责满洲国的工作。霍尔瓦特将军（General Horvath）的儿子是该公司在华北的管理委员会秘书。该公司的职员和大多数工人都是俄罗斯人。

鲁宾斯坦先生还是1913年中国政府发行的‘善后大借款’（Reorganization Loan）俄罗斯部分未付息票持有人的代表。为了确保这些息票的支付，他打算于12月22日前往南京，会见财政部代表，之后将前往华北旅行。回到上海后，鲁宾斯坦先生将启程前往欧洲。

Appendix "B"

Translation from Russian newspaper "Shanghai Zaria",
December 31, 1936.

S.D. RUBINSTEIN AND GOLD IN CHINA.
On the eve of important negotiations in Nanking.

Our prominent compatriot Mr. S.D. Rubinstein,
who arrived in Shanghai from Japan recently, is still
staying in this city. He is a big financier and has
considerable interests in English and Anglo-Japanese
goldmining concerns in Manchoukuo, Korea and North
China.

In Shanghai a few days ago there arrived from
Japan Viscount Inouye, former minister, who is at
present Chairman of the Naval and Military Commission
of the House of Peers. Viscount Inouye represents
the interests of the Government in several large
privately owned mining enterprises including the "SEN
MAK KICHIO" (?) Goldmining Company in Manchuria and
North China. The interests of the British shareholders
of this undertaking are represented by Mr. S.D.
Rubinstein. Mr. Massenet also works for the same
company in the capacity of an engineer. Mr. Gadsby,
Counsellor of the British Embassy in Tokyo, also
arrived in Shanghai from Japan.

Viscount Inouye, Messrs Gadsby and S.D. Rubinstein
will leave for Peiping shortly in connection with the
affairs of the goldmining concern in question, after
which they will return to Shanghai. Here they will
investigate the possibilities of English and Japanese
capital combining, with the object of exploiting
China's mineral wealth. In connection with the above
they will later visit Nanking to negotiate terms of
an Anglo-Sino-Japanese cooperation.

译自俄文报纸《上海柴拉报》（Shanghai Zaria），1936年12月31日。

S.D. 鲁宾斯坦与中国黄金。
在南京重要谈判前夕。

我们杰出的同胞S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生最近从日本抵达上海，目前仍留居本市。他是一位大金融家，在满洲国、朝鲜和华北的英资及英日合资金矿企业中拥有重大利益。

几天前，前大臣井上子爵（Viscount Inouye）从日本抵达上海，他目前是贵族院海军和军事委员会主席。井上子爵代表政府在几家大型私营采矿企业中的利益，包括满洲和华北的‘仙麦吉乔’（SEN MAK KICHIO）(?)金矿公司。该企业的英国股东利益由S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生代表。马塞内特先生也以工程师身份为同一家公司工作。英国驻东京大使馆参赞加兹比（Gadsby）先生也从日本抵达上海。

井上子爵、加兹比先生和S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生将因上述金矿企业的事务 shortly 前往北平，之后他们将返回上海。在这里，他们将调查英日资本结合的可能性，目的是开发中国的矿产资源。鉴于上述情况，他们随后将访问南京，就英中日合作条款进行谈判。

S. RUBINSTEIN SOLD THE CHOSEN CORPORATION

LONDON TO REPORT.

Serge Rubinstein, Director of the Chosen Banking
Corporation, is returning to London after a prolonged
stay in Japan in order to attend the annual meeting of
the company, which will be held some time towards the
end of this year.

It was reported recently that the corporation

Details of the transaction have not been published.
Rubinstein is now proceeding to London to make a
report at the said annual meeting of shareholders.

It is believed that the concern has been sold
for Y.12,000,000.

The capital of the Chosen Corporation amounted
to £725,000 and was made up of £10 shares.

During the course of last years the Corporation
paid out considerable dividends. The Corporation
was the actual owner of the KAPM Company (?) and
together with the Korean Coal Association also owned
a part of the capital of NURUPI (?).

S. 鲁宾斯坦将朝鲜公司出售给日本人并

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 17, 1937

RUBENSTEIN SEEKING
JAPANESE FUNDS
Proposed Consortium To
Finance Gold Mining
In North China

TOKYO, Feb. 16.—Discussions of possible Japanese participation in an international consortium for the financing of gold mining operations in North China to-day were under way between interests represented by M. Serge Rubenstein, banker of Paris and London, and a local group formed by the late Viscount Kyoshiro Inoue.
Accompanying M. Rubenstein is M. Jules Gilbert, who is in charge of the French interests in the Chosen Corporation as a director of the Franco-Asiatic Bank.
According to M. Rubenstein, Managing Director of the Chosen Corporation in London and of the Franco-Asiatic Bank in Paris, his interests own one of the most productive gold mines in Korea, employing approximately 3,000 men.
Apart from Korea, where four mines are in operation, the Chosen Corporation is also represented in North China and Manchoukuo. M. Rubenstein left yesterday for a tour of his company's holdings on the peninsula. He said he would probably proceed to Shanghai, from where he would fly to London.
A mine was opened in North China six months ago by the Chosen Corporation, which has been interested in the Far East for 12 years, according to M. Rubenstein.
The present negotiations, which are being handled by M. Gilbert in M. Rubenstein's absence, are expected to be concluded by the middle of March.—Domei.

东京，2月16日。—今天，由巴黎和伦敦银行家 Serge Rubenstein 先生所代表的利益方，与由已故井上恭四郎子爵组成的当地团体之间，正在进行关于可能由日本参与组建一个国际财团、为华北金矿开采作业提供融资的讨论。
陪同 Rubenstein 先生的是 Jules Gilbert 先生，他作为法亚银行的董事，负责朝鲜公司中的法国利益事务。
据 Rubenstein 先生称，他是伦敦朝鲜公司的总经理以及巴黎法亚银行的总经理，他的利益方拥有朝鲜最高产的金矿之一，雇佣了约3,000名工人。
除了在朝鲜有四座矿井在运营外，朝鲜公司在华北和满洲国也有代表机构。Rubenstein 先生昨天离开，去巡视该公司在半岛上的资产。他表示，他可能会前往上海，并从那里飞往伦敦。
据 Rubenstein 先生说，朝鲜公司已在远东涉足12年，六个月前在华北开设了一座矿井。
目前的谈判由 Gilbert 先生在 Rubenstein 先生缺席期间处理，预计将在3月中旬结束。—多米尼通讯社。

“Svengali” Arrives In

TOKYO, Feb. 6.—(Domei).—M. Serge Rubenstein, a 28-year old international banker, today reaffirmed his intention to play the role of a modern Svengali to his cabaret-dancing Trilby, Miss Gloria Seiter, 19.

Interviewed by the press at the Imperial Hotel, where M. Rubenstein, the blonde dancer and her mother registered after their arrival from Kobe, last night, he declared that he was “embarrassed” by the rumors regarding their trip here.

“I intend,” he said, “to take Miss Seiter to Europe and make her one of the world’s greatest dancers.”

With tears in her mascara-shaded eyes, Miss Seiter joined in the protestations that they were “not eloping.”

“All I am thinking about is my career,” she said. “I want to become a great dancer in Europe. I have no time for love. I wish you wouldn’t misunderstand this situation.”

After a stay of several weeks here, Miss Seiter, who until this week appeared nightly in a popular Shanghai night club, will proceed to the United States.

M. Rubenstein, who is the Managing Director of the Chosen Corporation, will go to Korea for an inspection of properties owned by his concern.

格洛丽亚·赛特与国际银行家鲁宾斯坦坠入爱河；行李从酒店秘密运至“长崎丸”号

惊讶的管理层祝愿好运

爱情今晨找到了出路。格洛丽亚·赛特，静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）西罗夜总会娇小迷人的艺人，与来自巴黎的年轻国际银行家谢尔盖·鲁宾斯坦，在丘比特丹（Dan Cupid）的帮助下撤离上海，于上午9时安静地从日本邮船会社（N.Y.K.）韦赛德码头（Wayside Wharf）登上“长崎丸”号，驶往日本。

这是一次货真价实的私奔。

同行的第三人是赛特小姐的母亲。他们的目的地是东京，去找一位牧师或治安法官主持婚礼。

鲁宾斯坦先生不久前从欧洲突然出现在上海，他来远东经商，据信涉及与中国和日本政府的大额交易。为了消磨时间，他去了西罗夜总会。

在那里，他看中并赏识了赛特小姐，她是——或者说曾是——那里的一名舞女兼歌手。他产生了兴趣。

还没等你说出“Parkyakarkus”这个词，他就陷入了由赛特小姐的魅力引起的迷醉状态，并向她赠送贵重礼物。

最后他们决定结婚是唯一的解决办法，但为了保持私密，他们没有告诉西罗夜总会的管理层。鲁宾斯坦先生还提出支付一大笔钱，以解除赛特小姐的合同。

然而，管理层喜欢赛特小姐，不想让她离开。他们拒绝了。

行李被偷运出去

与此同时，鲁宾斯坦先生回到他一直入住的华懋公寓（Cathay Hotel），打包好属于赛特小姐及其母亲的所有行李，并将其偷偷运出酒店，装上定于上午9点启航的“长崎丸”号。

珠宝

鲁宾斯坦先生的父亲在革命前是俄国沙皇的银行家，该家族在逃往巴黎之前，得以将他们收藏的大量贵重珠宝带出该国。

S. D. RUBINSTEIN AND GOLD IN CHINA

On the eve of important negotiations in Nanking

Our prominent compatriot Mr. S. D. Rubinstein, who
arrived in Shanghai from Japan recently, is still
staying in this city. He is a big financier and has
considerable interests in the English and Anglo-Japanese
goldmining concerns in Manchoukuo, Korea and North
China.

A few days ago arrived in Shanghai from Japan
Viscount Inouye, former minister, who is at present
Chairman of the Naval and Military Commission of the
House of Peers. Viscount Inouye represents the interests
of the Government in several large privately owned
mining enterprises including the "SEN MAC KICHIO" Gold-
mining Company in Manchuria and North-China. The
interests of the British shareholders of this undertaking
are represented by Mr. S. D. Rubinstein. Mr. Massenet
also works for the same company in the capacity of
engineer. Mr. Gatsby, Counsellor of the British Embassy
in Tokyo, also arrived in Shanghai from Japan.

Viscount Inouye, Messrs. Gatsby and S.D. Rubinstein
will leave for Peiping shortly in connection with the
affairs of the goldmining concern in question, after
which they will return to Shanghai. Here they will
investigate the possibilities of English and Japanese
capital combining, with the object of exploiting China's
mineral wealth. In connection with the above they will
later visit Nanking to negotiate terms of an Anglo-Sino-
Japanese cooperation.

"We intend to create a large Anglo-Sino-Japanese Gold
Mining Undertaking with capital furnished by all three
countries concerned," said Mr. S. D. Rubinstein.

在南京重要谈判前夕

我们杰出的同胞 S. D. 鲁宾斯坦先生最近从日本抵达上海，目前仍逗留于此。他是一位大金融家，在满洲国、朝鲜和华北的英资及英日合资金矿企业中拥有重大利益。

几天前，前大臣井上子爵（Viscount Inouye）从日本抵达上海，他目前担任贵族院海陆军委员会委员长。井上子爵代表政府在几家大型私营矿业企业中的利益，包括满洲和华北的“SEN MAC KICHIO”金矿公司。该企业的英国股东利益由 S. D. 鲁宾斯坦先生代表。马塞内特先生（Mr. Massenet）也以工程师身份为同一家公司工作。英国驻东京大使馆参赞盖茨比先生（Mr. Gatsby）也从日本抵达上海。

井上子爵、盖茨比先生和 S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生将因上述金矿企业的事务 shortly 前往北平，之后他们将返回上海。在此，他们将调查英日资本结合的可能性，旨在开发中国的矿产资源。鉴于上述情况，他们随后将访问南京，就英中日合作条款进行谈判。

“我们打算建立一个大型的英中日金矿企业，资本由所有三个相关国家提供，” S. D. 鲁宾斯坦先生说。

Mr. S.D. Rubinstein is Chairman of the Governing Board
of a big goldmining corporation in Japan and Korea and,
besides, acts as Director-General of three financial con-
cerns in London and one in Paris.
He arrived from London to the Far East recently and intends
to remain here for another month, after which he will re-
turn to Europe, the main field of his activities.
Up to the current year the goldmining corporation which
Mr. Rubinstein plans to develop in the Far East, has been
active only in Japan and Korea. Now it is planned to in-
clude Manchoukuo and North China in the sphere of its acti-
vities.
Work was already started in North China during August last
under the supervision of Mr. Massenet, engineer, while a Rus-
sian engineer named Vodennikoff is in charge of the work in
Manchoukuo. General Horvath's son is Secretary of the Govern-
ing Board of the corporation in North China. The staff of the
corporation and the majority of workers are Russians.
Mr. Rubinstein is also the representative of holders of unpaid
coupons of the Russian part of the "Reorganization Loan" is-
sued by the Chinese Government in 1913.
In order to secure the payment of these coupons he intends to
proceed to Nanking on December 22, where he will interview re-
presentatives of the Ministry of Finance, after which he will
make a trip to North China . Upon his return to Shanghai Mr.Ru-
binstein will leave for Europe.

SERGE RUBENSTEIN.

Born at Kronstadt on 31.5.08. Son of Dimitri Rubenstein
and Stella nee Fichtenhdtz. Height 5'6 - 7"; complexion pallid
round face; cleanshaven, hair dark; unusually stout for a man of
his age; smart appearance (description furnished in January
1935).

Formerly an Austrian, now stateless.

First arrived in France in 1923 from England, where he had
been educated. He entered the Banque Franco-Asiatique in Paris
as secretary to the Managing Director and soon, with the help
and advice of his father, occupied a preponderating position in
this financial concern, which, until its liquidation soon after,
was known as the Banque Russo-Asiatique. In June 1932 he was
made a member of the Board of Directors of the Banque Franco-
Asiatique, which had been founded as a limited liability company
for commercial, industrial and real estate transactions in France
and abroad, but chiefly in Manchukuo. The Bank, however, was
believed to be unfavourably regarded in both Paris and London.
When, however, he was made a member of the Board of Directors
many shareholders protested as it was felt that both he and his
father were merely using the Bank as a convenient instrument for
dealing with several risky and adventurous undertakings.

In 1935 Serge Rubenstein was reported as the Managing Director
of the Chosen Corporation Ltd., 56 Moorgate, E.C.2. The
business of this firm was the exploitation of gold, silver and
other mines on the Chinese-Korean boundary. Those in charge of
the Corporation were said to be in very favourable relations with
the Government of Manchukuo.

Rubenstein was reputed to be an unscrupulous man in the City
of London and alleged to have been under suspicion of espionage
in France in 1933. His father is said to have been sentenced to
a term of imprisonment at Paris for heavy commercial frauds.
page_data.zh:
塞尔日·鲁宾斯坦（SERGE RUBENSTEIN）。

出生于喀琅施塔得（Kronstadt），出生日期为1908年5月31日。季米特里·鲁宾斯坦（Dimitri Rubenstein）与斯特拉（Stella，娘家姓 Fichtenhdtz）之子。身高5英尺6至7英寸；面色苍白，圆脸；面部无须，黑发；对于其年龄而言异常肥胖；衣着整洁（描述提供于1935年1月）。

原为奥地利人，现为无国籍人士。

1923年从英国首次抵达法国，他曾在英国接受教育。他在巴黎进入法亚银行（Banque Franco-Asiatique）担任总经理秘书，并在父亲的帮助和建议下，很快在该金融机构中占据了主导地位，该机构在不久后清算前被称为俄亚银行（Banque Russo-Asiatique）。1932年6月，他成为法亚银行董事会成员，该银行作为一家有限责任公司成立，旨在进行法国及海外的商业、工业和房地产交易，但主要是在满洲国。然而，据说该银行在巴黎和伦敦均不受好评。然而，当他成为董事会成员时，许多股东提出抗议，因为人们认为他和他的父亲仅仅是利用该银行作为处理几项风险性和投机性事业的便利工具。

据报道，1935年塞尔日·鲁宾斯坦担任位于伦敦市Moorgate街56号（E.C.2）的朝鲜公司有限公司（Chosen Corporation Ltd.）的总经理。该公司的业务是开发中朝边境的金、银及其他矿山。据说负责该公司的人员与满洲国政府关系非常良好。

鲁宾斯坦在伦敦金融城被认为是一个肆无忌惮的人，并被指控于1933年在法国受到间谍嫌疑。据说其父亲因重大商业欺诈罪在巴黎被判入狱。

No.1052/ S.

OBJECT: Franco-Manchurian Bank.
Messrs. RUBINSTEIN, MASSERET and GUILBERT.

REFERENCE: Foreign Commercial Establishments in Shanghai.
Communication No. 135 dated April 9, 1936 from the
French Consulate-General.

The "Franco-Manchurian Bank" was opened in Shanghai
on March 15, 1936 by Mr. S.D. RUBINSTEIN, a Jew of Russian
origin, now a naturalised Portuguese.

This bank is located in Room. 309 on the third
floor of the Glen Line Building, 2 Peking Road - telephone
10679. The room in question is divided into two or three
offices which have the appearance of being only of a temp-
orary nature. When taking over these premises, Mr. Rub-
instein refused to sign any contract, and pays his rent
($220), monthly.

The staff of this organisation comprises only a
stenographer, Mrs. V.A.SHLIVANOVSKY, who resides at No. 2,
Passage No. 640, Avenue Joffre. She also acts as Rubins-
tein's secretary and was recommended to him by Mr. KAHN,
exchange broker and financial expert, who is well-known in
Shanghai.

In March last, during the course of a conversation
with Mr. YAVINSKY, a former director of the Russo-Asiatic
Bank, Rubinstein stated that the capital of the Franco-Man-
churian Bank was about Jap. 1,500,000.

The information at our disposal does not permit
us to state exactly whether this is a question of the
transfer to Shanghai of the administrative offices of an
already established Bank, or the creation, pure and simple,
of a new concern.

事项：法满银行。
鲁宾斯坦（RUBINSTEIN）、马塞雷（MASSERET）和吉尔伯特（GUILBERT）诸位先生。

参考：上海的外国商业机构。
法国总领事馆1936年4月9日第135号公函。

“法满银行”于1936年3月15日由 S.D. 鲁宾斯坦先生在上海开业，鲁宾斯坦是一名俄裔犹太人，现为归化葡萄牙人。

该银行位于北京路2号格兰轮船公司大楼（Glen Line Building）三楼309室——电话10679。该房间被分隔成两三个办公室，看起来只是临时性质的。在接管这些 premises 时，鲁宾斯坦先生拒绝签署任何合同，并按月支付租金（220美元）。

该机构的工作人员仅有一名速记员 V.A. 谢利瓦诺夫斯基夫人（Mrs. V.A.SHLIVANOVSKY），她居住在霞飞路640弄2号。她还担任鲁宾斯坦的秘书，是由在上海颇有名气的兑换经纪人和金融专家卡恩（KAHN）先生推荐给他的。

去年3月，在与俄亚银行前董事亚温斯基（YAVINSKY）先生的一次谈话中，鲁宾斯坦表示，法满银行的资本约为150万日元。

我们要掌握的信息不允许我们确切说明这究竟是将一家已成立银行的行政办公室迁至上海，还是纯粹简单地创建一家新公司。

2

Rubinstein:

S.D. RUBINSTEIN is the son of D.L. Rubinstein, internationally known financier, famous in Russia prior to the Revolution for his speculations.

The elder Rubinstein, who among other enterprises founded the Franco-Russian Bank at Petrograd, recently passed away in Zagreb (Yugoslavia.)

The younger Rubinstein is one of the directors of the Franco-Asiatic Bank which was created in Paris following the failure of the "Russo-Asiatic." This bank has two branches, one in Tokyo, which is directed by Mr. Alfred MASSENET (1) and the other at Harbin. The director of the latter branch, Mr. M.D. BOUIANVOSKY, committed suicide several months ago in Harbin, and it is thought in Russian circles there that his death was brought about by the bad state of affairs of the bank.

In 1932, when Rubinstein was in Europe, he was informed by a friend that if he had a million francs to dispose, he could acquire in London the control of an excellent gold-mine in Korea - "Chosen Syndicate," formed by Mr. MENDES.

Rubinstein, who could only muster Frs. 300,000, obtained the balance of Frs. 700,000 from the Franco-Asiatic Bank, on whose behalf he had to complete the negotiations (2).

The friend, whom we do not know sent Rubinstein to the London banker □□□□ who, as the holder of stocks of many companies and in particular of those of □□□□□ had an account in his bank from one of the major banks established, which as is known is also interested in the Chosen Syndicate.

2

鲁宾斯坦：

S.D. 鲁宾斯坦是 D.L. 鲁宾斯坦之子，后者是国际知名的金融家，在革命前的俄罗斯以其投机活动而闻名。

老鲁宾斯坦除其他企业外，曾在彼得格勒创立了法俄银行，最近在南斯拉夫萨格勒布去世。

小鲁宾斯坦是法亚银行的董事之一，该银行是在“俄亚银行”破产后在巴黎成立的。该银行有两个分行，一个在东京，由阿尔弗雷德·马塞内特（Alfred MASSENET）(1) 先生领导，另一个在哈尔滨。后一分行的行长 M.D. 布伊安沃斯基（BOUIANVOSKY）先生几个月前在哈尔滨自杀，当地俄国圈子认为他的死是由该银行糟糕的经营状况导致的。

1932年，当鲁宾斯坦在欧洲时，一位朋友告诉他，如果他有一百万法郎可供支配，他可以在伦敦获得一家位于朝鲜的优质金矿——“朝鲜辛迪加”（Chosen Syndicate，由门德斯 MENDES 先生组建）的控制权。

鲁宾斯坦只能凑出30万法郎，他从法亚银行获得了剩余的70万法郎，他必须代表该银行完成谈判 (2)。

这位我们不认识的朋友将鲁宾斯坦介绍给伦敦银行家 □□□□，后者作为许多公司股票的持有者，特别是 □□□□□ 的股票持有者，在一家主要银行开有账户，众所周知，该银行也对朝鲜辛迪加感兴趣。

page_data.en:
3

1) from Harman or his group, 125,000 "Chosen" for cash.
2) at the same time, on credit, 125,000 "Chosen" which
Harman had sold for 15/- to certain Japanese com-
panies, and promised to pay 16/6d. for them. Thus
he got possession of 250,000 shares at an average at
of 12/3d.

With the 125,000 shares purchased from Harman
Rubinstein with another stockbroking concern, created a
market for the stock, which rapidly rose in value, per-
mitting him to pay the Japanese companies the extra 1/6d.
per share.

Later, Rubinstein acquired an option on about
170,000 new shares at 22/- which made his total holdings
about 420,000. The amount of stock he is at present
carrying is unknown, but it is reported that he owns at
least two-thirds of "Chosen" stock.

The advantage over other shareholders conferred
on him by virtue of the amount of stock in his possession
allowed Rubinstein to "call himself" the managing-director
of the "Chosen" Mines to the tune of an annual salary of
a million francs plus his travelling expenses.

After these financial operations Rubinstein made
his way to Korea. The other holders of stock, especially
English holders, furious at being "skinned" in this manner
had an engineer sent to the "Chosen" Mines in order to
examine them and make a report discrediting their worth.
This report, made public, would have had the effect of
lowering the value of the shares, thus permitting the
English shareholders to recoup themselves by buying stock
that Rubinstein could not fail to place upon the market.
Indeed the report was published and the shares fell.
But Rubinstein, however, was not to be daunted by this show
of strength, and on the contrary, profited still more than
in price by buying more shares instead of selling his own
for during his stay in Korea he bought more shares.

3

1) 从哈曼（Harman）或其集团处，以现金购买 125,000 股“朝鲜”（Chosen）股票。
2) 同时，以赊购方式买入 125,000 股“朝鲜”股票，这些股票是哈曼以 15 先令的价格卖给某些日本公司的，并承诺以 16 先令 6 便士的价格回购。因此，他以平均每股 12 先令 3 便士的价格获得了 250,000 股的所有权。

利用从哈曼处购买的 125,000 股，鲁宾斯坦（Rubinstein）与另一家证券经纪公司合作，为该股票制造市场，使其价值迅速上涨，从而使他能够向日本公司支付每股额外 1 先令 6 便士的款项。

后来，鲁宾斯坦获得了以 22 先令购买约 170,000 股新股的选择权，使其持股总量达到约 420,000 股。他目前持有的股票数量不详，但据报道，他至少拥有“朝鲜”股票的三分之二。

凭借其所持股票数量赋予他的优于其他股东的优势，鲁宾斯坦得以“自封”为“朝鲜”矿业公司的总经理，年薪高达一百万法郎，外加差旅费。

在进行完这些金融操作后，鲁宾斯坦前往朝鲜。其他股票持有人，尤其是英国持有人，因被如此“剥皮”而愤怒不已，派遣了一名工程师前往“朝鲜”矿场进行检查，并出具一份贬低其价值的报告。这份报告一旦公开，将导致股价下跌，从而使英国股东能够通过购买鲁宾斯坦不得不投放市场的股票来挽回损失。事实上，报告确实发布了，股价也随之下跌。然而，鲁宾斯坦并未被这种示强举动所吓倒，相反，他通过购买更多股票而非抛售自己的股票，在价格上获得了比之前更多的利润，因为他在朝鲜停留期间购买了更多股票。

to gather information regarding the yield of the mine,
which was in the neighbourhood of ¥160,000 per month.
Later, he was responsible for having another report
made, favouring the "Chosen" Mine by Mr. A. MASSENET,
a well-known engineer, who was acting in good faith.
The results of this report were soon forthcoming, and
the value of the "Chosen" stock went up. This series
of operations thus brought Rubinstein a very considerable
profit.

It should be stated, however, that Rubinstein
enjoys the reputation of being an astute speculator. He
was expelled from France in 1935 for speculating in francs
but the expulsion decree was rescinded some months later
following pleas made on his behalf.

Coming from Europe Rubinstein arrived in Shanghai
on February 10, 1936 via Japan and Harbin. He stayed at
Room No. 513 Cathay Hotel, which was reserved for him by
Mr. E Allis HAIM of the Cathay Land Co., who has known
Rubinstein for a lengthy time. Towards the end of Feb-
ruary Rubinstein was joined by Mr. Massenet from Japan.
The latter put up at the same hotel, Room. No. 502.

During his stay in Shanghai Rubinstein had bus-
iness transactions with the following persons, also resid-
ing at the Cathay Hotel:-

John COSBY, J.C. CRAHAR and Jean GUILBERT. Exact
information regarding these people is unavailable.

Rubinstein with Guilbert left Shanghai on March 8,
for New York via Vancouver by the s.s. "Empress of Japan."

Leaving on the same vessel for the United States
was the Countess Sonja HENIE, aged 24, Norwegian,
Rubinstein's girlfriend, who arrived in Shanghai on February
28 on the s.s. "President Coolidge" and stayed at the Cathay
Hotel.

以收集有关矿产量的信息，该矿月产量约为 160,000 日元。后来，他负责促成由著名工程师 A. 马塞内特（A. MASSENET）先生出具的另一份报告，该报告对“朝鲜”矿场有利，且马塞内特先生是出于善意行事的。这份报告的结果很快显现，“朝鲜”股票的价值随之上涨。这一系列操作 thus 为鲁宾斯坦带来了非常可观的利润。

然而，必须指出的是，鲁宾斯坦享有精明投机者的声誉。他曾于 1935 年因投机法郎而被驱逐出法国，但在为其求情后，几个月后驱逐令被撤销。

鲁宾斯坦从欧洲出发，经由日本和哈尔滨，于 1936 年 2 月 10 日抵达上海。他住在华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel）513 号房间，该房间由华懋地产公司（Cathay Land Co.）的 E·阿利斯·海姆（E Allis HAIM）先生为他预订，海姆先生认识鲁宾斯坦已久。2 月底，马塞内特先生从日本赶来与他会合。后者入住同一家酒店的 502 号房间。

在上海停留期间，鲁宾斯坦与同样居住在华懋饭店的以下人士进行了商业交易：

约翰·科斯比（John COSBY）、J.C. 克拉哈尔（J.C. CRAHAR）和让·吉尔伯特（Jean GUILBERT）。关于这些人的确切信息无法获取。

鲁宾斯坦与吉尔伯特于 3 月 8 日离开上海，乘坐“日本皇后号”（s.s. "Empress of Japan"）轮船经温哥华前往纽约。

同船前往美国的还有索尼娅·赫尼（Sonja HENIE）伯爵夫人，24 岁，挪威人，鲁宾斯坦的女友，她于 2 月 28 日乘坐“柯立芝总统号”（s.s. "President Coolidge"）轮船抵达上海，并入住华懋饭店。

that the "Franco-Manchurian Bank" has been created by

et simple d'un établissement nouveau.

Ci-dessous quelques renseignements sur M. RUBINSTEIN:

S.D. RUBINSTEIN est le fils de D.L. RUBINSTEIN, financier
international bien connu en Russie avant la révolution, pour
ses spéculations.

RUBINSTEIN père qui a fondé, entre autres, à Pétrograd, la
Banque Franco-Russe, est récemment décédé à Zagreb (Yougoslavie)

RUBINSTEIN fils est l'un des directeurs de la Banque Franco
Asiatique qui fut créée à Paris à la suite de la faillite de la
"Russo-Asiatique". Cette banque a deux succursales, une à Tokio,
qui serait dirigée par M. Alfred MASSENET (1) et l'autre à Har-
bine. Le directeur de cette dernière agence, Mr.N.D.BOUIANVOSKY,
s'est suicidé il y a quelques mois à Harbine et sa disparition
est rattachée, dans les milieux russes, aux affaires peu bril-
lantes, paraît-il, de la banque.

En 1932, RUBINSTEIN qui se trouvait à ce moment-là, en
Europe, fut averti par un ami que s'il pouvait disposer d'une
somme de un million de francs, il pourrait acquérir à Londres
le contrôle d'une excellente mine d'or en Corée ("Chosen Syn-
dicate", créé par M. MONDON).

RUBINSTEIN qui n'aurait disposé alors que de 300.000 frs.
aurait obtenu le complément - 700.000 francs - de la Banque
Franco-Asiatique pour le compte de laquelle il devait faire
l'opération. (2)

以下是关于鲁宾斯坦先生的一些情报：

S.D. 鲁宾斯坦是 D.L. 鲁宾斯坦之子，后者是革命前俄国著名的国际金融家，以其投机活动闻名。

老鲁宾斯坦曾在彼得格勒创立了法俄银行等机构，最近在南斯拉夫萨格勒布去世。

小鲁宾斯坦是法亚银行的董事之一，该银行是在“俄亚银行”破产后于巴黎成立的。该银行设有两家分行，一家在东京，据称由阿尔弗雷德·马塞内特（Alfred MASSENET）(1) 先生主管；另一家在哈尔滨。哈尔滨分行的经理 N.D. 布伊安沃斯基（N.D. BOUIANVOSKY）先生几个月前在哈尔滨自杀，据俄罗斯圈子的人士称，他的死与该银行似乎不太光彩的业务有关。

1932 年，当时身处欧洲的鲁宾斯坦接到一位朋友的通知，称如果他能筹集一百万法郎，就可以在伦敦收购一家位于朝鲜的优质金矿的控制权（“朝鲜辛迪加”，由蒙东（MONDON）先生创立）。

当时鲁宾斯坦仅拥有 300,000 法郎，他从法亚银行获得了剩余的 700,000 法郎，代表该银行进行此项操作。(2)

L'ami que nous ne connaissons pas, l'aurait alors adressé
au banquier londonien HARMAN qui, détenteur d'actions de plusieurs affaires et en particulier de celles du "Chosen", aurait eu en dépôt dans sa banque des fonds importants de ces diverses sociétés qu'il aurait dilapidé et qu'il aurait cherché à rembourser en négociant les actions dont il était porteur.

Au moment où RUBINSTEIN rencontra HARMAN les actions du
"Chosen" auraient été cotées environ 7 shillings. Moyennant
un million, RUBINSTEIN aurait acheté:
1) à HARMAN ou à son groupe, 125.000 actions du "Chosen",
payées comptant.
2) En même temps, il aurait acheté à termes, les 125.000 actions que HARMAN avait vendues pour 15/ à certaines sociétés japonaises et s'engageait à les payer 16/6 d. Ainsi les
250.000 actions lui revenaient en moyenne à 12/3 d.

En possession des 125.000 actions achetées à HARMAN (I)
il aurait organisé, avec une maison de courtiers, un marché
qui aurait amené rapidement une hausse sur les actions, ce qui
lui aurait permis de rembourser les compagnies japonaises avec
un bénéfice de 1/6 d. par action.

Par la suite, RUBINSTEIN aurait acquis une option sur environ 170.000 nouvelles actions à 22/ qui lui aurait assuré
un total d'environ 420.000 actions.

Nous ignorons le nombre d'actions dont il est actuellement porteur mais on dit en tous cas, qu'il aurait en main et bien à lui les 2/3 des actions du "Chosen".

(I) HARMAN qui aurait employé au paiement, par la vente de ses actions, les fonds nécessaires pour éviter la ruine des poursuites contre lui, aurait été néanmoins condamné. Il se trouverait actuellement en prison.
page_data.zh:
1052/4-3.

这位我们不认识的朋友随后将他介绍给伦敦银行家哈曼（HARMAN），哈曼持有包括“朝鲜”在内的多家企业的股票，并在其银行中存有这些不同公司的大量资金，但他挥霍了这些资金，并试图通过谈判出售其持有的股票来偿还。

当鲁宾斯坦遇见哈曼时，“朝鲜”股票的报价约为 7 先令。鲁宾斯坦以一百万法郎的价格购买了：
1) 从哈曼或其集团处，以现金支付购买 125,000 股“朝鲜”股票。
2) 同时，他以远期方式购买了哈曼以 15 先令卖给某些日本公司的 125,000 股股票，并承诺以 16 先令 6 便士支付。因此，这 250,000 股股票的平均成本为 12 先令 3 便士。

在拥有从哈曼处购买的 125,000 股股票后 (I)，他与一家经纪公司组织了一个市场，导致股价迅速上涨，这使他能够以每股 1 先令 6 便士的利润向日本公司还款。

随后，鲁宾斯坦获得了以 22 先令购买约 170,000 股新股的选择权，这使他的持股总量达到约 420,000 股。

我们不知道他目前持有多少股票，但据说他手中确实拥有“朝鲜”三分之二的股票。

(I) 哈曼曾希望通过出售股票所得资金来避免被起诉而破产，但仍被判刑。他目前据说在监狱中。

1052/3 - 4.

L'avantage sur les autres actionnaires que lui confère-
rait le nombre d'actions qu'il porterait, lui aurait permis de
"se nommer" contrôleur des mines du "Chosen" aux appointements
annuels d'un million de francs plus ses frais de déplacements.
Après ces opérations, RUBINSTEIN se serait rendu en Corée.
Les autres détenteurs d'actions, surtout les anglais, furieux
de s'être vus dépouillés de la sorte, auraient dépêché un ingé-
nieur aux mines du "Chosen" pour lui faire établir sur ces mi-
nes un rapport les discréditant. Ce rapport, rendu public, de-
vrait faire baisser les actions, permettant ainsi aux action-
naires anglais de racheter celles que RUBINSTEIN ne manquerait
pas de mettre sur le marché. Le rapport aurait été en effet
publié et les actions auraient baissées. Cependant, RUBINSTEIN
ne se serait pas laissé prendre à ce stratagème et aurait pro-
fité au contraire de cette baisse pour racheter d'autres ac-
tions au lieu de vendre les siennes, car il aurait eu le temps,
pendant son séjour en Corée, de se renseigner sur les rapports
de la mine qui seraient dans les environs de 160,000 Yen par
mois. Il aurait fait ensuite établir, à son tour, un nouveau
rapport en faveur du "Chosen" par Mr. A. MASSENET qui serait un
ingénieur connu et qui agirait de bonne foi. Les résultats ne
se seraient pas fait attendre et les actions auraient remonté.
Cette opération aurait procuré à RUBINSTEIN une autre occasion
de faire de jolis profits.
Notons qu'en général, RUBINSTEIN jouit d'une réputation de
spéculateur astucieux. Il aurait été expulsé de France en 1935,
pour ses spéculations contre le franc. Le décret d'expulsion
aurait cependant été annulé quelques mois plus tard, à la suite
de certaines interventions.
page_data.zh:
1052/3 - 4.

他所持有的股票数量赋予了他优于其他股东的优势，这使他得以“自封”为“朝鲜”矿场的监理，年薪一百万法郎，外加差旅费。
在这些操作之后，鲁宾斯坦前往朝鲜。其他股票持有人，尤其是英国人，因被如此剥夺财产而愤怒，派遣了一名工程师前往“朝鲜”矿场，让他就这些矿场出具一份使其信誉扫地的报告。这份报告一旦公开，应会导致股价下跌，从而使英国股东能够回购鲁宾斯坦势必投放市场的股票。事实上，报告确实发布了，股价也下跌了。然而，鲁宾斯坦并未落入这一圈套，反而利用这次下跌回购了其他股票，而不是抛售自己的股票，因为他在朝鲜停留期间有时间了解矿场的产量，据悉每月约为 160,000 日元。随后，他又让知名工程师 A. 马塞内特（A. MASSENET）先生出具了一份有利于“朝鲜”的新报告，马塞内特先生是出于善意行事的。结果立竿见影，股价回升。这次操作为鲁宾斯坦提供了另一个赚取丰厚利润的机会。
值得注意的是，总体而言，鲁宾斯坦享有精明投机者的声誉。1935 年，他因针对法郎的投机活动被驱逐出法国。然而，经过某些干预，驱逐令在几个月后被撤销。

page_data.en:
1052/S.- 5.

Venant d'Europe, RUBINSTEIN est arrivé à Shanghai, le 10
Février 1936, Via Japon-Harbine. Il est descendu au Cathay Ho-
tel, ch.N°513 réservée pour lui par l'intermédiaire de M.Ellis
HAIM, de la Cathay Land C° Ltd, qui connaîtrait RUBINSTEIN de-
puis longtemps.

Vers la fin du mois de Février, RUBINSTEIN a été rejoint
par M. MASSON qui, venant du Japon, est descendu dans le
même hôtel, ch. N°502.

Pendant le séjour de RUBINSTEIN à Shanghai, il a été en
relations d'affaires avec les personnes suivantes qui habitai-
ent également le Cathay Hotel:

John COGSBY, J.C. CRAMAR et Jean GUILBERT. Nous n'avons
pu obtenir des renseignements précis sur leur compte.

RUBINSTEIN, accompagné de J. GUILBERT, a quitté Shanghai
le 9 Mars, à bord de l'"Empress of Japan", à destination de
New-York Via Vancouver.

A bord du même bateau est parti pour les Etats-Unis la
Comtesse Nathalie ERDOUY, Hongroise, 24 ans, "amie" de RUBINS-
TEIN, arrivée à Shanghai le 25 Février, à bord du "Kashima
Maru" et descendue au Cathay Hotel, ch.713.

RUBINSTEIN serait sous peu de retour à Shanghai. Sa cor-
respondance adressée au Cathay Hotel,est transmise à la "Banque
Franco-Mandchoue".

Ajoutons, pour terminer, que la "Banque Franco-Mandchoue"
aurait été créée par RUBINSTEIN pour faciliter ses opérations
avec les actions du "Chosen", car la situation financière de la
Banque Franco-Asiatique serait quelque peu compromise (1).

page_data.zh:
1052/S.- 5.

鲁宾斯坦（RUBINSTEIN）自欧洲出发，经日本、哈尔滨，于1936年2月10日抵达上海。他下榻于华懋饭店（Cathay Hotel），513号房间由华懋地产有限公司（Cathay Land C° Ltd）的埃利斯·海姆（Ellis HAIM）先生代为预订，据称海姆先生与鲁宾斯坦相识已久。

2月底，马松（MASSON）先生从日本前来与鲁宾斯坦会合，并入住同一家酒店的502号房间。

在鲁宾斯坦逗留上海期间，他与同样居住在华懋饭店的下列人士有业务往来：

约翰·科格斯比（John COGSBY）、J.C. 克拉马尔（J.C. CRAMAR）和让·吉尔贝特（Jean GUILBERT）。我们未能获得关于他们的确切情报。

3月9日，鲁宾斯坦在让·吉尔贝特的陪同下，乘坐“日本皇后号”（Empress of Japan）轮船离开上海，经温哥华前往纽约。

同船前往美国的还有匈牙利籍的纳塔莉·尔多伊伯爵夫人（Comtesse Nathalie ERDOUY），时年24岁，系鲁宾斯坦的“女友”。她于2月25日乘“鹿岛丸”（Kashima Maru）抵达上海，并下榻于华懋饭店713号房间。

鲁宾斯坦不久后将返回上海。寄至华懋饭店给他的信件，均转交至“法满银行”（Banque Franco-Mandchoue）。

最后补充一点，据称“法满银行”系由鲁宾斯坦创立，旨在便利其进行“朝鲜银行”（Chosen）股票的交易操作，因为法亚银行（Banque Franco-Asiatique）的财务状况已略显窘迫(1)。
